topIssues.title: op-reth v1.11.0 tls issue
topIssues.author: bhaveshtank
topIssues.body:
**Bug Description**

The `op-reth` binary from the OP Labs Docker image (`us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth:v1.11.0`) fails to connect to the flashblocks WebSocket endpoint with the error `"URL error: TLS support not compiled in"`. 

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Pull the OP Labs op-reth image: `docker pull us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth:v1.11.0`
2. Run op-reth with flashblocks enabled using `--flashblocks-url wss://<flashblocks-endpoint>/ws` on Optimism Mainnet
3. Observe the repeating WARN log every 5 seconds: `Error receiving flashblock err=URL error: TLS support not compiled in`

**Expected behavior**

op-reth should successfully establish a WSS connection to the flashblocks endpoint and receive flashblock data for building pending state.

**Environment Information:**

- Operating System: Linux (Docker)
- Docker Image: `us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth:v1.11.0`
- Package Version: op-reth v1.11.0
- Chain: Optimism Mainnet

**Configurations:**

```
--flashblocks-url wss://<flashblocks-endpoint>/ws
```

**Logs:**


topIssues.title: op-reth tx-pool admits transactions that can never be included on OP chains (missing op-geth EffectiveGasLimit / l1InfoGasOverhead reservation)
topIssues.author: asdv23

topIssues.title: op-reth tx-pool balance check omits the Isthmus operator fee (admits under-funded txs; op-geth parity)
topIssues.author: asdv23
topIssues.body:
### Summary

`OpTransactionValidator::apply_op_checks` (`rust/op-reth/crates/txpool/src/validator.rs`) reserves only the **L1 data fee** when checking that a sender can afford a transaction:

```rust
let cost_addition = l1_block_info.l1_tx_data_fee(self.chain_spec(), self.block_timestamp(), &encoded, false)?;
let cost = valid_tx.transaction().cost().saturating_add(cost_addition);
if cost > balance { /* InsufficientFunds */ }
```

It does **not** reserve the **Isthmus operator fee**. So on a post-Isthmus OP chain, a sender whose balance covers `L2 gas + value + L1 data fee` — but not the operator fee — is admitted to the pool and then fails at execution, wasting pool space / propagation.

`operator_fee` does not appear anywhere in `rust/op-reth/crates/txpool` (grep: 0 hits).

### op-geth parity

op-geth's txpool **does** charge the operator fee in its balance check: `NewOperatorCostFunc` / `NewTotalRollupCostFunc` (`core/types/rollup_cost.go`), combined via `TotalTxCost` and used in `ValidateTransactionWithState` (`core/txpool/validation.go`), guarded by the operator-fee hardfork activation. op-reth is therefore behind op-geth on single-tx pool admission.

### Proposed fix

In `apply_op_checks`, when the operator fee is active, add `l1_block_info.operator_fee_charge(&encoded, U256::from(gas_limit))` to `cost_addition`.

Guarding is required: `L1BlockInfo::operator_fee_charge` (`op-revm`) `.expect()`s both `operator_fee_scalar` and `operator_fee_constant`, so it panics when they are unset (pre-Isthmus). Gate on Isthmus activation (`is_isthmus_active_at_timestamp`) **and** both params being `Some`. Use the tx `gas_limit` (worst-case spend), matching op-geth's `tx.Gas()`. This is pool-admission only — no block-validation / state-root / execution change.

### Related

Sibling tx-pool admission gap in the same validator: #21546 / #21548 (missing `l1InfoGasOverhead` / `EffectiveGasLimit` reservation).

Note: a **cumulative** variant also exists in reth-core (`PoolInternalTransaction::next_cumulative_cost` sums the intrinsic `cost()`, which omits both L1 fee and operator fee) — that is a separate reth-core concern and is not covered here.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: port op-succinct fault-proof proposer (create path)
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Ports succinctlabs/op-succinct's fault-proof proposer (`fault-proof` crate @ [`13716c2c`](https://github.com/succinctlabs/op-succinct/tree/13716c2ca316babb41d92369bd7bb0312611ed5f/fault-proof)) into `rust/kona/sp1/crates/proposer` as `kona-sp1-proposer`: the Rust proposer for the super-root `ZKDisputeGame` (game type 10). PR 1 of two: **create path** (game creation, resolution, two-phase bond claiming). The **defend path** (challenge detection, proof requests, `prove()`) follows under #21463.

Part of #21414 (create path; #21414 stays open until the prove() interaction lands in PR 2, #21463). Supersedes #21995 (the Go op-proposer adaptation): `op-proposer/` is untouched here and gets deprecated after the ZK upgrade, per team decision that one Rust application should own propose+prove. The proposer-agnostic pieces of #21995 (`gameargs.ParseZK`, `ZKGameImpl` parser cutover, `WaitForZKGameCount` DSL) are salvaged into this PR.

### Port fidelity

The runtime skeleton (pinned-L1 sync discipline, game DAG + canonical head selection, task scheduler, backup, cursor walk) is a **near-verbatim port** - 90-100% line-identical after mechanical renames - so upstream fixes to that machinery can be cross-applied by diff. Adaptation is confined to the contract/data-source seams:

- **Claims from the supernode**: `superroot_atTimestamp` supplies the super-root proof preimage, root claim (`keccak256(proof)`), and safe/finalized timestamp views gating cadence (`PROPOSAL_SAFETY=safe|finalized`). `SuperRootAtTimestampResponse` in `super-range-executor` gains the safe/finalized fields the Go server already serves.
- **extraData** = `parentIndex (4B BE) || superRootProof`; UUID-collision handling advances the timestamp (fresh proof fetch each step), bounded by the safety limit.
- **Discovered-game validation** against the canonical super root; a timestamp that is not yet safe locally is *pending* (excluded from parent selection, re-validated each sync, persisted across restarts) rather than terminally dropped - this also structurally prevents the far-future-parent liveness stall flagged in #21995's security review.
- **Catch-up cadence**: a head lagging by more than one interval proposes at the newest proposable timestamp instead of crawling across the gap (restart after downtime, devstack time warps).
- **Identity**: op-succinct's aggregationVkey/rangeVkeyCommitment/rollupConfigHash triplet collapses to `absolutePrestate()` (the super-aggregation program vkey, `PROGRAM_VKEY` env) + `verifier()`.
- **Two-phase DelayedWETH claiming**: unlock once finalized, payout once the withdrawal delay elapses **in L1 time** (chain time, not wall time - they diverge under devstack time travel).
- **Not ported** (deliberate): `challenger.rs` (op-challenger owns challenge/close, #21983), `prover.rs` + all proving config (PR 2), sp1-cluster + GCP KMS dependencies, alt-DA features, the anvil test harness (devstack supersedes it).

### Devstack / acceptance

The ZK preset now starts the real proposer (first env-configured sysgo service; `LOG_FORMAT=json` so the readiness matcher can parse the startup line) unless `SkipHonestProposer`. The four pre-existing ZK lifecycle tests keep manual control via `WithoutHonestProposer()`. One CI change: the `RUST_BINARY_PATH_KONA_SP1_PROPOSER` export (the workspace build already produces and persists the binary).

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p kona-sp1-proposer --lib`: 21 tests (canonical-head DAG selection incl. catch-up chains, proposal timing incl. catch-up rule, bounded collision walk, pending-game parent ineligibility, two-phase claim state machine + chain-time maturity, backup schema guard, GameStatus/ProposalStatus enum pins vs Types.sol, 140-byte gameArgs decode with the same vectors as Go's gameargs tests, extraData encoding with #21995's vectors).
- Acceptance (verified locally, real binary + contracts + supernode, all PASS): `TestProposerCreatesRootZKGame`, `TestProposerChainsSecondZKGameOnFirst`, `TestProposerResolvesOwnUnchallengedGame`, `TestProposerClaimsBondAfterResolution` (full unlock -> delay -> payout cycle).
- Regression: the four pre-existing ZK lifecycle tests pass; `just lint-go` clean; clippy/fmt clean; `git diff -- op-proposer/` is empty; `op-e2e/system/proofs` (Go proposer) passes.
- In a long local run the binary chained 51 games (root at parentIndex uint32.max, then 0 -> 1 -> ... -> 50) and self-resolved 49 of them.

## Notes for reviewers

- Textual overlap with #21983 (challenger) in `multichain_proofs.go` and the ZK acceptance setup; whichever lands second rebases. The merged ZK devstack branch should start both the challenger and this proposer.
- `ZKDisputeGame.sol` was derived from the older op-succinct commit `c13844a9`; this port tracks `13716c2c`.
- Plan: `.claude/plans/2026-07-24-feat-kona-sp1-proposer-port-plan.md` (local).

topPRs.title: op-deployer: build continuation deploy input from prepared state
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

`op-deployer` builds continuation deployment inputs from prepared state. Permissionless chains use their committed game type, selected prestate, and complete starting-anchor proposal. Later game type or prestate changes are rejected.

`CANNON_KONA` uses the fixed permissioned fallback. `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` has no fallback prestate. Permissioned deployments keep existing behavior.

Missing or incompatible prepared values fail before execution. Re-running `prepare` clears the starting anchor for chains it predicts again. Deployed chains keep their state.

The same completed input can be used for preflight and deployment. Deployment is recorded separately, allowing `continue` to record only after broadcast succeeds.

**Tests**

Covers game types, prepared-state authority, fallbacks, invalid state, chain binding, anchor transport and resets, permissioned compatibility, execution and recording, and deployed configuration.

**Additional context**

Replaces #21610. This PR is stacked on #21611 and must merge `develop` after #21611 merges.

A preceding stage supplies the starting-anchor proposal. #21669 will add the `continue` command's whole-deployment preflight, broadcast, retry, and verification flow.

**Metadata**

Closes #20912

topPRs.title: op-devstack,op-acceptance-tests: extract reusable SDM acceptance harness for external suites
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #21958 — review/merge that first.

Makes the SDM acceptance tests drivable from outside this repo, so
optimism-premium can boot its own sequencer binary against the same
fixtures instead of forking them.

- **New importable `sdmtest` package** — the `RethSystem` fixture
  (op-reth sequencer + verifier + batcher + funder on one Interop/SDM
  chain), the repeated-slot warming workload that drives PostExec (`0x7D`)
  txs, and the SDM opt-in / client-version RPC helpers. Non-test so
  out-of-tree suites can import it; the monorepo never depends on them.
- **Generic external-binary seam** — drops the hardcoded `op-reth-premium`
  kind/helper. A CLI-superset binary is selected per-node via
  `OpRethWithBinary` + `RUST_BINARY_PATH_<NAME>`, applied after the shared
  options so one node can take a flag its peers reject.
- **`OpRethWithoutProofsHistory`** — opts a single node out of proofs-history
  (some superset binaries reject `--proofs-history` in certain modes).
- **`DEVSTACK_MONOREPO_ROOT`** — lets an out-of-tree consumer point at a
  monorepo checkout for contract artifacts.
- Refactors the existing SDM tests onto the shared package; removes the
  redundant `helpers_test.go` and `premium_baseline_test.go`.

No change to in-repo coverage — the same tests run the same way against
stock op-reth. The seam is purely additive.

topPRs.title: op-proposer: create super-root ZK dispute games
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Teach op-proposer the ZKDisputeGame (game type 10) create path (closes #21414, first slice of #21463). The defend path (challenge detection, proof requests, prove/resolve) is out of scope and stays in #21463.

- **Parent selection.** `SelectZKParent` walks factory games newest to oldest with paged multicall reads and picks the first parent `ZKDisputeGame.initialize()` would accept. Challenged-but-undecided parents are legal parents; refusing to build on locally-invalid games is defend-path policy (#21463 / #21445).
- **extraData.** ZK proposals submit `create(10, superRootHash, parentIndex || superRootProof)`. The root claim is unchanged supernode output (`keccak256(superRootProof)`). A tick is skipped when the safe timestamp is not strictly beyond the starting sequence number, so an honest proposer can never hit the `initialize()` ordering revert.
- **Single decision point.** `proposalExtraData` is the only place the game-shape decision is made; non-ZK game types keep the exact previous encoding (locked by a unit test), and the proposal log now reports the bytes actually submitted.
- **gameargs.ParseZK** (inverse of `Pack`); the devstack `ZKGameImpl` hand parser is replaced with it.
- **Config.** Game type 10 joins `postInteropGameTypes`, requiring a super-root RPC
- **Devstack + acceptance.** ZK presets now start the production proposer with game type 10 (honoring `SkipHonestProposer`); the four existing lifecycle tests opt out to keep manual control. Three new acceptance tests drive the real binary.

## Test plan

- `go test ./op-proposer/...` and `go test ./op-challenger/game/fault/contracts/gameargs/...`: 11 `SelectZKParent` cases (including a cross-page walk), driver ZK branch tests, extraData goldens, ZK ABI added to the `HasProposedSince` compatibility table, `ParseZK` round trip.
- Acceptance (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs/zk`, verified locally): `TestProposerCreatesRootZKGame`, `TestProposerChainsSecondZKGameOnFirst`, `TestProposerCreatedGameResolvesDefenderWon` all pass: the real proposer creates a root game, chains a second on it with a strictly increasing sequence number, and the game resolves `DEFENDER_WINS` and anchors.
- Regression: the four pre-existing ZK lifecycle tests pass (now with the honest proposer explicitly disabled); `op-e2e/actions/proposer` passes (non-ZK create path unchanged end to end).

## Notes

- Tiny conflict with #21983 (challenger side) in `multichain_proofs.go` and the ZK acceptance setup; whichever lands second rebases. The merged ZK devstack branch should start both the challenger and the proposer. After #21983 lands, `TestProposerCreatedGameResolvesDefenderWon` should switch from manual `Resolve` to waiting on the honest challenger's resolution.
